title: When Overwhelm'd with Grief
description: When Overwhelm'd with Grief in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 61, headed “Safety in God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When o-ver-whelm'd with grief My heart with-in me dies, Help-less and far from all re-lief To heaven I lift mine eyes.

lines: Helpless and far from all relief
To heaven I lift mine eyes.
O lead me to the rock
And make the covert of thy wings
Thou art the tower of my defence,
Of those that fear thy Name;
If endless life be their reward,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
